title: Memoization with functools.lru_cache

kcs.statement: @functools.lru_cache(maxsize=N) stores results keyed by the call's arguments and returns the stored result on repeat calls; maxsize=None, or functools.cache, makes it unbounded.
lru_cache requires every argument to be hashable; calling a cached function with a list argument raises TypeError.
A cached function's cache_info() reports hits, misses, maxsize and currsize, and cache_clear() empties the cache.

problem_ideas: Predict the number of calls for naive fib(20) versus cached fib(20)
Predict cache_info() after fib(10) with lru_cache(maxsize=None)
Explain the TypeError from a cached function called with a list and fix it with a tuple
Predict evictions for maxsize=2 after calls f(1), f(2), f(1), f(3), f(2)
Spot why f(1) and f(1.0) share a cache entry but f(1, typed=True) settings differ
Write a minimal dict-based @memoize and compare it to lru_cache
